items.training: • Training effect (HRV focus): 5–10 minutes at an easy, equal in/out pace.

dialItIn.title: Smooth over deep
dialItIn.body: Slide between 3–8 s per phase. Start small. Smooth > deep. If holds feel edgy, skip them and keep an even inhale/exhale.

items.nasal: • Breathe nasal and quiet; feel low belly rise.
items.exhale: • Exhale ends softly. Don't squeeze empty.

items.hrv: • Slow breathing can increase vagally mediated HRV during sessions.
items.exhale: • Exhale-emphasized or 0.1 Hz pacing often feels calmer within minutes.
items.consistency: • Consistency matters; short daily sessions beat rare long ones.

nextLinks.title: Where to go next
nextLinks.intro: Start with the page that matches your situation: a quick reset, an app-style timer, a running recovery guide, or an advanced meditation technique.

precision.title: Precision breathwork.
precision.body: Press Start and follow the orb through inhale, pause, exhale, pause. The cadence is adjustable. Sessions are short. Effects are tangible.

calmByDesign.body: Slow, even breathing often increases vagally mediated HRV and lowers perceived stress during practice.

builtForRealLife.body: Short sets (1–5 min) before meetings, between tasks, or at lights-out.

yourPace.body: Choose 3–8 seconds per phase. Smaller, quieter breaths beat "big" breaths.

quickAnchor.title: One minute to steady
quickAnchor.intro: Sit tall. Shoulders soft. Tongue to the roof of your mouth. Inhale gently through the nose; exhale quietly through the nose or pursed lips.

bullets.easy: • Keep it easy. If dizzy, shorten phases or pause.
bullets.nasal: • Breathe nasal and quiet; feel the low belly rise.
bullets.exhale: • Exhale ends softly. Don't squeeze empty.

quickAnchor.closing: Dial in a smooth cadence, then keep breathing. Small, steady breaths trump deep gasps.

howLong.question: How long should I practice?
howLong.answer: Start with 60–120 s. If it's still easy and helpful, extend to 3–5 min. For HRV-focused training, 5–10 min most days.

bestTime.question: When's the best time?
bestTime.answer: Before a meeting or workout, between blocks of deep work, or before bed. Use physiological sighs for urgent spikes of stress.

timing.question: Can I change the timing?
timing.answer: Yes. That's the point. Use 3–8 s per phase. If holds feel uncomfortable, remove them and keep an even inhale/exhale.

lightHeaded.question: What if I feel light-headed?
lightHeaded.answer: You're likely over-breathing. Make breaths smaller and quieter, shorten phases, or pause and breathe normally.

medical.question: Is this medical treatment?
medical.answer: No. It's a self-regulation tool. If you have a cardiopulmonary condition, are pregnant, or have fainting history, avoid long holds and keep everything gentle.
